rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the next experiment should test a foundational multimodal configuration to establish baseline performance. Config_016 tests multimodal fusion (concat) with pca_n2000 and resnet50, which are simple yet representative choices. This clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform unimodal ones and identifies if fusion method (concat vs weighted) matters, while keeping computational cost low.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, which is a critical design choice. Since fusion methods significantly impact multimodal models, this test clarifies if weighted fusion offers better integration of RNA and image features. It balances exploitation (building on the existing multimodal setup) and exploration (testing a key hyperparameter variation).

The existing evidence shows that using resnet50 and pca_n2000 with concat fusion achieves ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with a more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other parameters (singleprofile, pca_n2000, concat fusion) consistent. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice is critical for performance, addressing a key design decision with minimal changes to the proven baseline.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_022) outperforms resnet50, and concat fusion (config_016) is better than weighted fusion. However, all prior experiments use singleprofile. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (a common method) and concat fusion, which could reveal if profile setting or aggregation type significantly impacts performance. It balances exploration of multiprofile (a key design choice) and exploitation of proven components (imagenet_vit_l, concat).

Existing evidence shows config_024 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves high validation accuracy (0.6287). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted (config_025) improves performance, clarifying the importance of fusion methods in multiprofile settings. It directly extends the current high-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of known strengths and exploration of critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while retaining weighted fusion could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of aggregation methods on model effectiveness. This is a logical extension of the current high-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of promising design choices with exploration of critical hyperparameters.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the same successful configuration to determine if RNA encoder choice impacts performance. It clarifies the importance of RNA encoder design while building on a proven effective framework.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation with the same encoders and weighted fusion could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of aggregation methods. It is the best next step as it explores a critical design choice (aggregation) with potential to yield significant gains.

The existing evidence shows that models using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high performance (e.g., config_039: 0.725 accuracy). This experiment tests whether using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion (as in config_039) impacts performance, clarifying the importance of fusion method. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a key design choice (fusion type) with minimal changes to the proven high-performing components.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether scgpt, a different RNA encoder, can match or exceed this performance in the same setup, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current promising direction (transformer + weighted fusion) with exploration of a new encoder, providing critical insights under limited budget.
